摘要

財報背後的算力焦慮與現金流赤字

騰訊最新財報顯示，該公司連續兩季出現高達829億元的自由現金流赤字，這是騰訊超過二十年來首見的單季現金流轉負情況。作者解釋，雖然騰訊在帳面上仍有數百億元的淨利潤，但由於為了規避美國商務部限制以獲取海外算力，騰訊選擇迂迴擔保無關聯公司代為租賃，導致律師、合規與營運等中介成本飆升。面對阿里巴巴、百度與華為的競爭，騰訊預判未來算力成本將持續上漲，因此即便背負鉅額前期支出，也必須提前大手筆注資以確保算力無虞。

「海陸分流」說辭與內部創新的殘酷本質

在騰訊二十八週年之際，創辦人馬化騰罕見發表嚴厲言論，警告核心業務正面臨危機潮水，隨後市場便傳出裁員50%的傳聞。騰訊公關與高層雖解釋這是將員工分為守衛舊業務的「陸軍」與探索AI新戰場的「海軍」，但作者以過去在盛大創新院的切身經驗直言，大企業內部打著「創新開拓」旗號的分流，往往代表該批人員缺乏資源與重視，本質上就是即將被組織優化的前兆，很難在體制內部真正獲得成功。

AI進展全面落後與部門藩籬的掣肘

作者指出，騰訊當前最大的危機在於AI時代的全面落後。相較於字節跳動「豆包」與阿里巴巴「通義千問」擁有的千萬級日活躍用戶，騰訊自家推出的元寶表現未達預期，旗下的混元大模型在獨立評測中亦落後於Kimi。更嚴峻的是，騰訊內部山頭林立，微信、QQ、遊戲與雲服務等部門彼此防備競爭，導致AI無法打通底層數據與聊天脈絡。相較於Meta能將Meta AI無縫整合進WhatsApp與Instagram並串連商務生態，騰訊的AI產品在自家生態中處處受限，陷入難以施展拳腳的尷尬境地。

AI進展全面落後與部門藩籬的掣肘

Later , we realized that tools like Feishu and DingTalk had captured the office market , and Tencent wanted a piece of the action too, but couldn't get anything off the ground. Finally, WeChat said, " You guys aren't cutting it, watch me," and launched WeCom. It took off instantly and is now one of China’s top three office suites, along with DingTalk and Feishu. But why is WeCom so effective? Because it’s part of the WeChat ecosystem.

Even though they’re all under Tencent, WeChat guards its territory. It allows for Video Accounts and WeCom, but if you want to tap into WeChat's traffic or social graph for other projects, it’s a no-go. You can’t get it, and nobody else can either—only they can access it. Now, regarding AI, WeChat has a trump card: "Xiaowei." It can access chat logs , Moments, official accounts, and video content. The first is to break down these internal silos—to issue an order, pull the social graphs from WeChat and QQ,. and concentrate all resources on AI. This could actually work. Look at Meta’s Llama; they were behind, but once they caught up, people loved it because they integrated the whole system . Grok did the same by integrating with X , and Google’s Gemini connects Workspace , Gmail, and everything else. It all depends on whether Tencent is willing to take that step. If they do, they can keep their momentum. going for a while. And what is the other path? The other path is the Amazon route— where their AI is a bit of a mess. Amazon isn't without AI; they have it, and they even use it within their site to help drive sales. But it’s just bad, truly terrible. It’s the same thing; my core business is just too strong, and I absolutely cannot let this go. It’s not safe—the reasoning is always the same. But then, Amazon did something else, didn’t they? I invested. in IC, pouring in a huge amount of money . After that, I built data centers and rented them to Anthropic, effectively becoming a fundamental infrastructure provider. That’s the identity I’ve taken on. I have a profitable e-commerce business on top, and I’m a major shareholder in the most valuable AI company, who also buys my computing power. That’s the state it’s becoming. Tencent might end up in a similar state . I have WeChat, games, QQ, and all.

these stable money-making businesses—no problem there. There might be some downsizing, but they can still earn for a long time. Then I invest, like in MiniMax. In several of DeepSeek’s major funding rounds, Tencent has been a lead investor . Then I buy computing power and lease it back to firms like MiniMax or DeepSeek. Is this a viable path for me to take? No problem at all; it’s a path that can work. Many people ask, "Wait, isn't this. a guaranteed win?""Why does Old Fan say they’re definitely going to die?" It’s like this: when they have a path that offers a guaranteed win, and they try to strive for more on top of that, it will never work out. When they have a surefire way to make money during times of rapid change, they effectively fall behind. You can be their shareholder or provide computing power, but looking ahead, are your services truly irreplaceable? Not necessarily. Once these AI firms really grow, they won’t necessarily rely. on you anymore. If you hold onto the mindset of just sitting back and collecting rent, the motivation to break through silos and disrupt yourself from within diminishes . So, the probability of them failing remains very, very high. Let’s sum it up . Tencent has shown us today just how conflicted and painful it is for a company that was once successful—a company that has seen better days—to face new opportunities and challenges.
